quote: I'm the one that did that before him. He doesn't know yet.
stewart_read: Karen states plainly that Eric — the named lead and likely co-owner — has no idea this inquiry or call is happening. This is the single most important co-decision-maker fact on the call, and the rep does not follow up on it at all.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't register the significance and moved straight into verify questions. Strategic read would require evidence the rep deliberately deferred this to closer's handoff — no such evidence exists (rep never revisits Eric's awareness at any point, including button-up).
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to flag this immediately: 'Since Eric's the one on the account, let's make sure he's looped in before Saturday — is he going to be available too?' This should have been asked before locking the appointment, not left for the closer to discover.

quote: We're looking for solar panels for our home and garage. I've got to detach. I have no electricity.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a detached, unpowered garage as a target for solar — an unprompted, highly specific use-case signal that increases system size and value. Rep acknowledges but never anchors on it again after this point.
coaching_implication: Manager should note this as a lead-quality signal the rep should have echoed back later ('so we'll design for the house and that detached garage you mentioned') to build curiosity and confirm scope, rather than letting it pass as a one-off verify answer.

quote: That's about $380 a month with a lot. Oh, wow. Why it's so high.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a strong bill-pain moment, including her own surprised reaction to the number — an open door for the flip (ask + acknowledge + flip). Rep validates emotionally but never converts the number into savings/action framing.
coaching_implication: Replay this clip: show the rep the gap between 'that's super high' (acknowledge) and the missing next line that should tie the $380 to the program's savings pitch.

quote: The last not last month, but month before, three months, it's, like, $700 a month.
stewart_read: A second, even larger bill figure ($700) surfaces late in the call with the customer expressing genuine confusion about the spike. This is a second bite at the bill-anchor apple and the rep again files it without using it to build curiosity about what the design could show her.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: appointment is already booked, so there's less urgency to flip it live. Strategic read would hold if rep tied the $700 forward to the appointment ('the specialist can dig into exactly why that spike happened'), but no such line appears.
coaching_implication: Coach: even post-booking, high-emotion numbers should be verbally tied to what the closer will show the customer — reinforces the appointment's value and reduces no-show risk.

quote: We can do Well, not a good day. I have plan for the day.
stewart_read: Initial proposed date (tomorrow) is rejected due to a conflict, and the booking process becomes a multi-minute back-and-forth with several false starts (April 30, evening, then finally Saturday 09:30) before landing.
coaching_implication: Not a rep failure — customer-driven scheduling friction — but the manager should note the multiple long holds (12:49, 14:43) as time-efficiency points to discuss for pacing, not persuasion.

quote: And let you know that my husband and I are deaf. I'm talking through a relay service.
stewart_read: Karen discloses a significant accessibility need for the in-home visit. Rep response is minimal ('That works. I'll go ahead and put that down for the notes here') with no acknowledgment of what this means for how the closer should prepare (e.g., confirming the relay/Google Translate setup in advance).
coaching_implication: This is a trust gift the rep under-responded to. Coach: a brief acknowledgment ('Thanks for telling me — I'll make sure the specialist knows how to communicate so the visit goes smoothly') would have been low-cost and high-trust.

quote: I thought the other financial plan where we can payment plan?
stewart_read: Customer asks a financing/payment-plan question post-booking. Rep answers with the standard credit-score-670 / no-out-of-pocket framing, which is appropriate setter-scope content already used earlier, not a new objection-inversion scenario.
alternative_hypothesis: This is not a fitting case for objection_inversion (schema explicitly scopes that pattern to cost/time/interest objections in the first 5 minutes); this is a post-booking curiosity question answered adequately within setter scope.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here — rep stayed within appropriate scope and gave a consistent answer to the financing question.
